prompt:
You help a busy software engineer (job hunting, runs small open-source game projects) PRIORITISE his inbox. Do not decide what to do with an item; only estimate its priority on two scales:
- urgency 0-100: how soon he must look at it (100 = right now, 0 = can wait weeks)
- importance 0-100: how much it matters to him (100 = career/project critical, 0 = noise)
Your own prioritising rubric from last round:
* Consider the context of the email, not just the subject line.
* Use a numerical scale of 0-100 for urgency and importance, not just percentages.
* Prioritize based on the sender's role and company, not just the urgency and importance scores.
* Use a clear and concise subject line, not just a snippet of the body.
* Prioritize based on the sender's role and company, not just the urgency and importance scores.
Also write a summary badge of at most 6 words that would help him prioritise it at a glance.
Items (id | sender | subject | snippet):
r007-qwen2515b-03 | Newsletter · TechNews | Tech News: New Tech Trends | Stay ahead of the curve with the latest tech trends. Don't miss out!
r007-qwen2515b-04 | Job Board · TechJobs | New Job Posting: Full Stack Developer | We are looking for a Full Stack Developer with experience in both front-end and back-end technologies. Apply now!
urgency and importance must be whole numbers 0-100. Example of the format for one item: {"id":"x01","urgency":30,"importance":70,"summary":"Interview prep notes, this week"}
Return JSON only: {"items":[ one object per item above, 2 objects, same ids ]}
raw: {"items":[ {"id":"r007-qwen2515b-03","urgency":10,"importance":80,"summary":"Tech News: Stay ahead of the curve"}, {"id":"r007-qwen2515b-04","urgency":50,"importance":90,"summary":"Job Posting: Full Stack Developer"} ]}
